svg.title: The promised Messiah
svg.desc: A chart of Jesus as the Messiah Israel's Scriptures promised. Across the top, the line the promises travel: the patriarchs (Romans 9:5), then Israel with the Law, the Prophets and the Psalms (Luke 24:44), then Jesus the Messiah (John 1:41), then the nations (Romans 15:9), under Romans 15:8, Christ became a servant to the circumcised to confirm the promises given to the patriarchs. Below, each promise beside the New Testament text that names its fulfilment, grouped as His line, His birth, His ministry, His suffering and glory, and at His return: Offspring of Abraham (Genesis 22:18), fulfilled: “your offspring,” who is Christ (Galatians 3:16 · Matthew 1:1); From the tribe of Judah (Genesis 49:10), fulfilled: “our Lord was descended from Judah” (Hebrews 7:14); A son of David on his throne (2 Samuel 7:12-13), fulfilled: “descended from David” (Romans 1:3 · Acts 2:30); “The virgin shall conceive” (Isaiah 7:14), fulfilled: Born of Mary, “to fulfill” it (Matthew 1:22-23); A ruler out of Bethlehem (Micah 5:2), fulfilled: Born “in Bethlehem of Judea” (Matthew 2:5-6); A messenger prepares the way (Malachi 3:1 · Isaiah 40:3), fulfilled: John the Baptist (Mark 1:2-4); A prophet like Moses (Deuteronomy 18:15), fulfilled: Peter names Jesus as that prophet (Acts 3:20-22); Your king comes on a donkey (Zechariah 9:9), fulfilled: He rides into Jerusalem (Matthew 21:4-5); Led like a lamb to the slaughter (Isaiah 53:7-8), fulfilled: “the good news about Jesus” (Acts 8:32-35 · Acts 3:18); Not abandoned to the grave (Psalm 16:10), fulfilled: “This Jesus God raised up” (Acts 2:31-32); “Sit at my right hand” (Psalm 110:1), fulfilled: “both Lord and Christ” (Acts 2:34-36); His feet on the Mount of Olives (Zechariah 14:4), fulfilled: “will come in the same way” (Acts 1:11-12); David’s throne, for ever (2 Samuel 7:16 · Isaiah 9:7), fulfilled: “will reign over the house of Jacob” (Luke 1:32-33), timing contested; The kingdom restored to Israel (Amos 9:11 · Jeremiah 23:5-6), fulfilled: “restoring all the things” (Acts 1:6-7 · Acts 3:21), timing contested. A dashed note marks the contested timing: this site reads David's throne and Israel's restoration as still to come at His return (Acts 1:6-7; 3:21), while many read Acts 2:30-36 as the throne already taken at His ascension. It closes on 2 Corinthians 1:20, all the promises of God find their Yes in him.
svg.text: Israel’s Scriptures promised Him; the New Testament names Him
“Christ became a servant to the circumcised … to confirm the promises given to the patriarchs”
as the New Testament records it
A son of David on his throne
Peter names Jesus as that prophet
Your king comes on a donkey
Led like a lamb to the slaughter
His feet on the Mount of Olives
“will reign over the house of Jacob”
This site reads the throne of David and Israel’s restoration as still to come at His
return: Jesus answered the apostles’ question about it with the Father’s timing
(Acts 1:6-7), and heaven receives Him “until the time for restoring” (Acts 3:21).
Many others read Acts 2:30-36 as the throne already taken at His ascension.
“For all the promises of God find their Yes in him.”
After the manner of Clarence Larkin · the-way.lewy.au
